forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let [n choose k]_q denote the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient. Prove that for all integers n, k, ℓ with 0 ≤ k, ℓ ≤ n, if [n choose k]_q / [n choose ℓ]_q is a polynomial in q, then it has only nonnegative coefficients.

forbidden_claims.label: lem_20260329120647_c4ea7dea
forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let a, b, r be integers with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0. Set I := {a+1, a+2, ..., b}, and let R := Q[x_s : s in I] be the polynomial ring graded by deg(x_s) = s for each s in I. For each positive integer d define M_d(u,v) := |{m in Z : u < m <= v and d divides m}|. Assume M_d(r+a, r+b) >= M_d(a,b) for every positive integer d. Then there exists a family (f_s)_{s in I} of homogeneous polynomials in R such that deg(f_s) = r+s for every s in I, and the ordered list of these polynomials in increasing order of s is a regular sequence in R. If I is empty, this means the empty family.

forbidden_claims.label: lem_20260329110006_654a633e
forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let a, b, r, j be integers with 0 <= a <= b, r >= 0, and 0 <= j <= floor(r (b - a) / 2). Put I := {a+1, a+2, ..., b}. For each positive integer d, define M_d(u,v) := |{m in Z : u < m <= v and d divides m}|, and assume M_d(r+a,r+b) >= M_d(a,b) for every positive integer d. Let X_j be the set of pairs (S, lambda) such that S is a subset of I, lambda is a finite multiset of elements of I, |lambda| denotes the sum of the elements of lambda, and |lambda| + sum_{s in S} (r + s) = j. Then there exists an involution iota_j : X_j -> X_j such that: (1) if iota_j(S,lambda) = (S',lambda') != (S,lambda), then |S'| is congruent to |S| + 1 modulo 2; and (2) if iota_j(S,lambda) = (S,lambda), then |S| is even.

forbidden_claims.label: lem_20260329092547_6a64d34a
forbidden_claims.statement_nl: For integers a, b, r with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0, let q be an indeterminate, define (q;q)_n := product_{j=1}^n (1 - q^j) for n >= 0 with (q;q)_0 := 1, set R_{a,b,r}(q) := ((q;q)_{r+b} (q;q)_a) / ((q;q)_{r+a} (q;q)_b), and define D := r (b - a). Assume that R_{a,b,r}(q) belongs to Z[q]. Then for every integer j with 0 <= j <= floor(D/2), the coefficient of q^j in R_{a,b,r}(q) is a nonnegative integer.

forbidden_claims.label: lem_20260329074016_d9949d95
forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let a, b, r be integers with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0. Define P_{a,b,r}(q) := product_{i=a+1}^{b} ((1 - q^(r+i)) / (1 - q^i)), with empty product equal to 1. Assume that for every positive integer d one has floor((r+b)/d) - floor((r+a)/d) >= floor(b/d) - floor(a/d). Then P_{a,b,r}(q) is a polynomial in Z[q], and every coefficient of P_{a,b,r}(q) is nonnegative.

semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every choice of integers a, b, r with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0, if every positive integer d has at least as many multiples in the interval from r + a to r + b as in the interval from a to b, then for every positive integer d the number of indices i from 1 through b for which d divides e_i is at least the number of indices i from 1 through b for which d divides i.
quantifier_order: Fix integers a, b, r with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0.
For each integer i with 1 <= i <= b, define e_i by a piecewise rule: e_i = i if i <= a, and e_i = r + i if a < i <= b.
For each positive integer d and integers u, v, define M_d(u, v) as the number of integers m satisfying u < m <= v and d divides m.
Assume that for every positive integer d, M_d(r + a, r + b) is at least M_d(a, b).
Conclude that for every positive integer d, the number of indices i from 1 through b with d dividing e_i is at least the number of indices i from 1 through b with d dividing i.

payload.statement_nl: Let a, b, r be integers with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0. For 1 <= i <= b define an integer e_i by e_i = i when i <= a, and e_i = r+i when a < i <= b. For each positive integer d define M_d(u,v) := |{m in Z : u < m <= v and d divides m}|. If M_d(r+a, r+b) >= M_d(a,b) for every positive integer d, then for every positive integer d one has |{i in {1,...,b} : d divides e_i}| >= |{i in {1,...,b} : d divides i}|.

result_payload.proof_nl:
Fix an arbitrary positive integer d. Define
A := {i in {1,...,b} : d divides e_i}
and
B := {i in {1,...,b} : d divides i}.

We split the index set {1,...,b} into the disjoint union {1,...,a} union {a+1,...,b}. (If a=0 or a=b, one of these sets is empty, and the same argument still applies.) Therefore A is the disjoint union of A ∩ {1,...,a} and A ∩ {a+1,...,b}, and similarly for B.

For i with 1 <= i <= a, the definition gives e_i = i. Hence
|A ∩ {1,...,a}| = |{i in {1,...,a} : d divides i}|.

For i with a < i <= b, the definition gives e_i = r+i. The map i -> r+i is a bijection from {a+1,...,b} onto the set {m in Z : r+a < m <= r+b}. Under this bijection, the condition d divides e_i is exactly the condition d divides m. Thus
|A ∩ {a+1,...,b}| = |{m in Z : r+a < m <= r+b and d divides m}| = M_d(r+a,r+b).

Since the two pieces are disjoint,
|A| = |{i in {1,...,a} : d divides i}| + M_d(r+a,r+b).

Now do the same for B. Clearly,
|B ∩ {1,...,a}| = |{i in {1,...,a} : d divides i}|.
Also, the identity map is a bijection from {a+1,...,b} onto {m in Z : a < m <= b}, so
|B ∩ {a+1,...,b}| = |{m in Z : a < m <= b and d divides m}| = M_d(a,b).
Therefore,
|B| = |{i in {1,...,a} : d divides i}| + M_d(a,b).

By the hypothesis of the lemma, for this positive integer d we have
M_d(r+a,r+b) >= M_d(a,b).
Comparing the formulas for |A| and |B|, we obtain
|A| >= |B|,
that is,
|{i in {1,...,b} : d divides e_i}| >= |{i in {1,...,b} : d divides i}|.

Because d was arbitrary, this holds for every positive integer d, exactly as claimed.
result_payload.proof_summary: Fix d>0 and split the indices into 1<=i<=a and a<i<=b. On the first part, e_i=i, so the two divisibility counts are identical. On the second part, i -> r+i is a bijection from {a+1,...,b} to the integer interval (r+a,r+b], so the count of indices with d dividing e_i is M_d(r+a,r+b), while the count of indices with d dividing i is M_d(a,b). The assumed inequality M_d(r+a,r+b) >= M_d(a,b) then gives the desired conclusion.
